cyberattack: Other: Prompt injection across an agent-to-agent command boundary causing an unauthorized token transfer
data.description:
Previously reported by Bankr founder 0xDeployer on May 4, 2026, and analyzed by Giskard. This packet adds independent explorer-receipt checks; it does not claim discovery of an unreported incident. It concerns an attacker-induced transfer through Grok and Bankr.

Verified execution: BaseScan shows Success for transaction 0x6fc7eb7da9379383efda4253e4f599bbc3a99afed0468eabfe18484ec525739a at 2026-05-04 06:49:01 UTC (block 45543997). Its token log moves 3,000,000,000 DRB, contract 0x3ec2156D4c0A9CBdAB4a016633b7BcF6a8d68Ea2, from 0xB1058c959987E3513600EB5b4fD82Aeee2a0E4F9 to 0xE8E476bdd78b0aa6669509ec8d3e1c542d5a686b. These are token units, not a current-dollar loss estimate.

Mechanism and attribution: Bankr founder 0xDeployer's public May 4 explanation says a block on Grok replies did not survive an agent rewrite, allowing prompt injection to cause Grok to instruct Bankr to transfer funds. The wallet was automatically associated with Grok's X account; the founder says xAI was not managing it. This supports involvement of the Grok product, but not an exact model version or a claim that xAI corporate assets were stolen. Giskard's technical account describes an encoded-message lure. No attack was reproduced in this investigation.

Recovery: transaction 0x54b3aa1ac3dd997926dd84eaa6d6aeb10e6606d2c70117bdfd9a4df015915a50 succeeds at 10:01:07 UTC (block 45549760), returning 88,826 USDC to the Bankr-associated address. The founder reports 80% returned overall. Only this USDC return was independently checked; total recovery, proceeds, and net loss are not reconciled here.

Authorization: this is a successful third-party-induced transfer outside the intended command boundary. A malicious human requested the action indirectly. It is not evidence of an agent independently deciding to spend or seek money. Exact owner instructions and private execution logs remain unavailable.

Evidence checked October 21, 2026. On-chain facts were checked through explorer receipts, not an independent node. Original X URLs are supplied; their text was accessible through xitter.cf mirrors, whose authenticity is a limitation. Giskard is a secondary technical account. Sources, receipt facts, and verification limits are listed here; no full articles are reproduced.

SlowMist’s May 7 primary investigation clarifies that Bankr’s infrastructure executed the transfer and managed wallet custody. It describes centralized membership activation. This adds source detail, not a newly discovered incident; full recovery accounting remains unverified.
data.summary: May 4, 2026: a prompt-injection chain through Grok and Bankr moved 3 billion DRB on Base. The transfer and an 88,826 USDC return are verified; Bankr acknowledged the exploit. Attacker-directed, not spontaneous agent spending.
